name: Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect with Ventricular Hypoplasia
aliases: Complete AV Septal Defect with Ventricular Hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Complete AVSD with Ventricular Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of a complete atrioventricular septal defect with a common atrioventricular valve
Imaging confirmation of hypoplasia of one or both ventricles, typically the left ventricle
Presence of clinical signs consistent with congestive heart failure in neonates or infants
Characteristic systolic and diastolic murmurs detected on auscultation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of complete AV septal defect with common AV valve plus imaging evidence of ventricular hypoplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic and imaging findings; clinical signs support but are not definitive.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating cardiac strain
Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia in cyanotic cases
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating complete AV septal defect with common AV valve
Cardiac MRI or CT confirming ventricular hypoplasia and chamber morphology
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
other: Cardiac catheterization data for hemodynamic assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of separate mitral and tricuspid valves instead of common AV valve
Less extensive septal defect limited to atrial septum
Severe underdevelopment of left-sided cardiac structures without complete AV septal defect

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Progressive respiratory distress with poor feeding
